stem: A build pipeline for an internal application automatically downloads a package by name. An attacker publishes a public package with the same name and a higher version number, and one build resolves to the public source instead of the approved internal repository. What is the BEST software-development ecosystem control?
decision_point: make dependency resolution deterministic and constrained to approved sources with authenticated repositories, version or artifact controls, provenance and monitoring rather than trusting package names and latest-version selection
misconceptions: a unique internal package name cannot collide with public repositories
selecting the newest version is a security control
SCA alone determines whether the source repository was authorized

originality.authoring_note: Original development-ecosystem scenario focused on dependency resolution crossing an internal/public repository trust boundary.

options: Continue selecting the highest available version because newer packages are more likely to contain security fixes
Rename the application but leave package-resolution rules unchanged

Restrict dependency resolution to authenticated approved repositories or namespaces, pin or otherwise control expected versions and artifacts, verify provenance or integrity where appropriate, and monitor dependencies through the software supply-chain process
Disable all third-party libraries in every project because dependency risk cannot be managed
explanation: The core problem is an uncontrolled dependency-resolution trust boundary. Deterministic approved sources, authenticated repositories, artifact/version controls, provenance or integrity checks, and dependency monitoring reduce the opportunity for a public package to impersonate an internal dependency.
distractor_rationales: Version recency does not establish that a package came from an authorized source.
Changing the application name does not correct how the build system chooses dependency sources.

The core problem is an uncontrolled dependency-resolution trust boundary. Deterministic approved sources, authenticated repositories, artifact/version controls, provenance or integrity checks, and dependency monitoring reduce the opportunity for a public package to impersonate an internal dependency.
Third-party software can be governed; a blanket ban is usually unnecessary and does not address internally published components.

stem: A software security program reports success because the SAST scanner produces fewer findings than last year. At the same time, production incidents caused by authorization defects have increased, and developers frequently suppress scanner findings without documented review. What is the BEST way to assess software-security effectiveness?
decision_point: measure security outcomes and control operation across changes, suppressions, escaped defects, remediation and risk rather than using raw scanner finding count as the success metric
misconceptions: fewer scanner findings always mean more secure software
suppressed findings no longer need governance
production escape rates are unrelated to development-security effectiveness

originality.authoring_note: Original software-assurance measurement scenario contrasting a favorable tool-volume metric with worsening production security outcomes.

options: Continue using total SAST findings as the primary KPI because lower volume proves the codebase has fewer vulnerabilities

Measure risk-relevant outcomes and control operation, including escaped vulnerabilities, severity, recurrence, remediation time, suppression approvals, change traceability, and whether mitigations work; then use those results to improve the program
Disable the scanner so production incidents become the only source of software-security data
Automatically accept all developer suppressions because developers understand the code better than security tools
explanation: Software-security effectiveness is about whether risk is being reduced, not whether one tool emits fewer alerts. Outcome measures, governed suppressions, change evidence, recurrence, and remediation data show whether controls actually improve software security.
distractor_rationales: A lower finding count can result from weaker rules, exclusions, suppression, or changing coverage rather than improved security.

Software-security effectiveness is about whether risk is being reduced, not whether one tool emits fewer alerts. Outcome measures, governed suppressions, change evidence, recurrence, and remediation data show whether controls actually improve software security.
Removing an assessment source reduces visibility and does not improve underlying controls.
Suppressions can be valid, but they should be reviewable and governed because an incorrect suppression can hide real risk.

stem: A web application lets users submit a URL so the server can fetch a document and generate a preview. Developers block URLs containing 'localhost' and a short list of private IPv4 ranges, but attackers still reach internal services through alternate address representations and redirects. What is the BEST secure-coding improvement?
decision_point: design outbound fetch functionality around explicit allowed destinations and validated resolved targets with controlled redirect and network egress rather than trying to enumerate forbidden URL strings
misconceptions: blocking the literal string localhost prevents server-side request forgery
one-time URL syntax validation is sufficient after redirects
application input validation makes network egress restrictions unnecessary

originality.authoring_note: Original secure-coding scenario focused on SSRF defenses failing when based on string blacklists rather than positive destination and egress policy.

options: Add more text patterns for private addresses until every known representation is blacklisted
Allow any initial URL as long as the final HTTP response is a document
Move the URL-fetch feature to a larger server so malicious requests cannot exhaust resources

Define approved destination schemes and hosts or networks where the business permits it, validate resolved destinations and redirects against that policy, minimize the fetcher's privileges, and enforce outbound network restrictions as defense in depth
explanation: Negative string matching is brittle because addresses can be represented and redirected in many ways. A positive destination policy, validation of resolved and redirected targets, least privilege, and egress controls provide a stronger secure-design boundary for server-side fetching.
distractor_rationales: Blacklists are difficult to make complete across alternate encodings, DNS behavior, redirects, and address forms.
Redirects and the ultimate resolved destination are part of the security decision, not only the initial URL.
Additional capacity does not prevent unauthorized server-side access to internal or metadata services.

Negative string matching is brittle because addresses can be represented and redirected in many ways. A positive destination policy, validation of resolved and redirected targets, least privilege, and egress controls provide a stronger secure-design boundary for server-side fetching.

stem: A company plans to acquire a managed code-assistant service that can read private repositories and submit pull requests. The vendor provides strong general security documentation, but the contract is unclear about whether customer code may be retained for model improvement, which subprocessors receive repository content, and how generated changes are isolated between tenants. What is the BEST acquisition-security decision?
decision_point: evaluate the acquired service against the organization's software, data and access requirements and resolve material data-use, subprocessor, isolation, retention and assurance gaps contractually or technically before approving sensitive repository access
misconceptions: general vendor security documentation proves every service-specific use is acceptable
source-code access is low risk when the service only proposes changes
managed services shift all software-security responsibility to the provider

originality.authoring_note: Related to the prior SaaS development-platform acquisition scenario, but focuses on AI-assisted code access, model-improvement use, subprocessors, tenant isolation, and repository write capability.

options: Approve the service based solely on the vendor's general security documentation because managed services own all security decisions
Allow access to all repositories first and evaluate the service after developers report problems
Reject every managed development service categorically because third-party software cannot be assessed safely

Define the service-specific security, privacy, intellectual-property, repository-access, retention, subprocessor, isolation, logging, and incident requirements; obtain evidence and contractual commitments or technical restrictions that address them; then approve only the scoped use whose residual risk is acceptable
explanation: Acquired software and managed services should be evaluated against the organization's actual security requirements and intended use. General assurance is useful but does not resolve service-specific questions about code use, access, retention, subprocessors, tenant isolation, or change authority.
distractor_rationales: Provider documentation may support due diligence, but it does not automatically cover the customer's specific data, access, and contractual requirements.
Granting broad access before resolving material risks reverses the purpose of acquisition security review.
Third-party and managed services can be used when their risks and requirements are assessed and governed appropriately.

Acquired software and managed services should be evaluated against the organization's actual security requirements and intended use. General assurance is useful but does not resolve service-specific questions about code use, access, retention, subprocessors, tenant isolation, or change authority.
